items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Like George Foreman, 50 years old, if he has to have a fight, you think he wants to run ten miles? No way.

ctx.x: I’ll be darned. Well you really knew your mind, what you wanted to do.

I always wanted — it was something I wanted to learn. I almost had a nervous breakdown the first time I heard Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie. It was something so new to me, something I was looking for all my life. Because I had all this technique and didn’t know what to do with it. And my idols were Roy Eldridge and Lester Young. They played so pretty and simple. And I had all this technique. So I gave up playing vibes and playing drums. When I heard Bird and Diz I said what is that? Because they played all…

went back and played four million notes, maybe three were right. Maybe. But I knew the timing. I got the timing down. That was my whole life. Music has always been my whole life. So, Monk, seriously, I don’t even buy anything. I’m 76 years old now, with the body of a man 75, so, and the brain of a 19 year old idiot. If I didn’t like music — I am not a millionaire, but I’m okay. I don’t have to go anywhere anymore. I lucked out with land and all that. But the point I’m getting at is if I was in a band that didn’t…
